subject: Post-demo: streaming SLO sizing playbook for Elysius
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@elysius.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@elysius.ai
Date: 2027-05-23T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: streaming targets & dedicated fit

Thanks for the demo earlier today — helpful walkthrough. Quick recap/questions from our side:

- We expect 95th p95 latency target of <=180ms for 512-token streaming (server->client chunking) for our summarization path.
- Concurrent active sessions: peak 220, typical 100. Expected token/sec per session ~8 during streaming.
- We need reserved throughput guarantees for 10K tokens/sec burst for scheduled batch runs.
- Can you confirm recommended GPU families for cost/perf tradeoff (A100x-80GB, H100-80GB, and 80-bit quantized 4xA10)?

Attached is a sample trace (bench-outputs-05-23.log) and a toy prompt set. Next steps: an SLO sizing note and a small pilot to validate a dedicated pool. Can you send a short proposal we can share with procurement?

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Senior ML Eng, Elysius Health
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@elysius.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: streaming targets & dedicated fit

Sam — thanks for the clear notes and the trace. Quick answers + proposed next steps below.

- Latency: 180ms p95 for 512 tokens streaming is achievable with H100-backed reserved pools if you enable continuous batching + prefix KV caching. On A100s we typically see ~10-25% higher p95 depending on sequence shape.
- Concurrency: peak 220 active sessions aligns with a reserved slab with autoscale headroom. We'll propose initial sizing for 250 concurrent streaming sessions to give buffer.
- Throughput bursts: we can reserve slab capacity to guarantee 10k tokens/sec for batch windows; cost will depend on commit term.
- GPU recomm: H100 for lowest p95 and best mixed precision path. A100 is cost-effective for sustained batch throughput. A10/4x quantized is good for lower-cost inference but expect latency variance on streaming due to kernel maturity.

I'll attach a short SLO sizing sheet and a pilot checklist. Karthik — can you draft the SKU/price options and pilot run steps? Ben — can you add ops-runbook bullets for the pilot (metrics/tracing hooks we should capture)?

Attaching: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@elysius.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: streaming targets & dedicated fit

Matt — sorry small typo in the header (Mateo). Drafted SKU options below; note these are placeholder pricing to unblock procurement discussion:

Option A (performance): H100-reserved slab (2x H100 per slab) — SLO: p95 <=160ms @512 streaming tokens; reserved throughput 12k tok/s. Commit: 12 months.
Option B (balanced): A100 cluster (4x A100 pooled) — SLO: p95 <=220ms @512 tokens; reserved throughput 10k tok/s. Commit: 6 months.
Option C (cost): Quantized A10x4 nodes — best-effort streaming, p95 varies 220-400ms; reserved throughput 10k tok/s for batch windows only; Commit: monthly.

Pilot recommendation: 2-week pilot on a single slab (H100) to validate p95 and streaming tail behavior; collect traces + KV-cache warmup profile. For procurement, I'll translate into a short quote doc and share link to a draft.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@elysius.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: streaming targets & dedicated fit

Added ops checklist below and a short runbook for the pilot:

- Metrics to capture: token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end per chunk), KV hit rate, GPU util, kernel-level stall traces.
- Tracing hooks: attach request id -> HV trace; record batching window size and sequence length distribution.
- Acceptance gates: p95 <=180ms for 512 tokens observed over 48h with KV cache warmed; no more than 5% p99 spikes above 300ms.
- Rollout plan: start with H100 slab in us-west region, 72-hour smoke, then 2-week pilot with production traffic replay.

I'll spin up the runbook doc and share in Drive. Karthik — when you have the quote draft, drop the HubSpot link and I'll attach ops SOW.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
